review.summary: This paper evaluates annual 10m satellite foundation-model embeddings (AlphaEarth Foundations V1 and TESSERA v1) for screening one-year tree-cover transitions (tree gain from non-tree cover and tree loss from tree cover) in the conterminous United States (CONUS) using human-interpreted LCMAP reference plots (2017-2021) and an Annual NLCD Collection 1.0 extension (2020-2023). Specifically, given the initial cover class, the study tests whether adjusting a fixed start-year forest-reference similarity difference score via year-matched reference centroids or independent control-plot mean subtraction improves classification at transferred 10% false-positive rate thresholds compared to cosine change magnitude and supervised classifiers. Across all primary conditions, reference and control adjustments produce negligible, inconsistent changes in Youden's J (-0.037 to +0.011), leave 90.8-98.5% of alert decisions unchanged, and flip signs across alternative calibration splits because continental reference centroids move very little over one year and global control subtraction is constant within each region-year. More interestingly, the study uncovers a stark asymmetry between one-year tree loss and gain: while cosine change magnitude strongly detects tree loss (AUROC 0.956-0.968), it detects 0 of 24 LCMAP gains at the calibrated threshold and ranks tree-gain plots below unchanged grass/shrub negatives (AUROC 0.287-0.352). In contrast, subsequent-state reference similarity, supervised classifiers, and even initial-year-only classifiers achieve substantially higher gain discrimination, indicating that one-year dominant-cover gains in LCMAP largely reflect plots already near the tree threshold at the start date. While the empirical diagnostics and statistical honesty are strong, the study is limited by a tiny tree-gain sample size (24 positives, with only 3 in 2020-2021), a one-year horizon ill-suited to gradual tree growth, continental-scale reference pools ~1,000 km away, and dense, caveat-heavy prose.

score_reasons.correctness: All empirical claims, algebraic identities, and boundary checks are rigorously supported by exact counts and uncertainty intervals, and the text carefully avoids overclaiming beyond its narrow one-year conditional setup.
score_reasons.verifiability: The paper documents exact public data sources, score equations, calibration percentiles, seeds, and full contingency counts across 35 pages, marred only by an unfinished paired-native AlphaEarth COG check.
score_reasons.novelty: While the algebraic scores and sklearn classifiers are standard, benchmarking both AlphaEarth and TESSERA on transferred thresholds and demonstrating the cosine-magnitude ranking inversion on one-year tree gains versus initial/subsequent-state scores are solid empirical contributions.
score_reasons.generality: Generalizability is severely constrained by having only 24 tree-gain positives (21 in a single year pair), evaluating one-year intervals rather than multi-year regrowth trajectories, and using broad reference pools located a median of >1,000 km away.
score_reasons.usefulness: Provides a valuable practical warning for remote-sensing teams that raw annual embedding-change magnitude fails to flag one-year tree gains and demonstrates why subsequent-state and initial-date-only baselines must be checked in conditional change tasks.
score_reasons.clarity: The manuscript reads like a defensive technical audit log saturated with repetitive disclaimers, internal repository file paths, and unnumbered tables and figures, making the narrative needlessly difficult to follow.

research_question.question: In CONUS one-year land-cover pairs with known initial cover classes, do year-matched reference centroids or control-plot mean adjustments improve tree-cover gain and loss screening over a fixed start-year reference score, cosine change magnitude, and supervised classifiers?
research_question.predictable_reason: The null effect of continental reference/control adjustments (where region-year control subtraction is an exact constant offset preserving rankings) and the advantage of multi-dimensional supervised learners were predictable from algebra and study design, whereas the inversion of cosine change magnitude on one-year tree gains (AUROC ~0.30) was a non-trivial empirical finding.

main_issues.issue: Extremely small tree-gain sample size and one-year temporal horizon: The primary LCMAP test set contains only 24 gain positives (21 in 2019-2020 and just 3 in 2020-2021), and the 2022-2023 NLCD extension has only 7. Moreover, because ecological tree gain takes multiple years, one-year dominant-cover transitions mostly capture plots already near the tree/shrub boundary in the start year (as shown by the high accuracy of the before-only classifier), which does not test multi-year restoration trajectories.

Mismatch between continental reference/control pooling and ecological reference designs: Selecting only 58 reference and 58 control plots across CONUS places the 8th-nearest reference a median of 1,071 km away. Averaging ~40-50 distant forest plots across a continent yields minimal year-to-year centroid drift, and subtracting a single region-wide control mean is algebraically guaranteed not to change within-region/year rankings, making the primary adjustment test a strawman for local BACI or reference-ecosystem matching.

Audit-log writing style and formatting flaws: The text is overly telegraphic and repetitive, interrupting nearly every paragraph with defensive caveats and internal repository file paths (e.g., scripts/prepare.py, protocol/plan-v1.md, analysis/nlcd-initial-v17) that are inaccessible to readers of the PDF. Several tables and figures lack numbers or captions, and the y-axis label ('Youden's J') on the page 23 figure is partially clipped.

Unfinished paired-native AlphaEarth check: The primary AlphaEarth evaluation relies on an unofficial geographic mosaic (tge-labs) with latitude-varying pixel footprints, and the planned 16-pair native-grid COG comparison failed to complete (0/16 complete pairs obtained), leaving only a 20-pair single-date substitution check.

High threshold-transfer noise across calibration partitions: Because operating thresholds are set at the 90th percentile of small earlier-year negative subsets, all 8 primary reference/control J contrasts reverse sign across the 10 exploratory fitting/calibration cell-split perturbations (Appendix F), indicating that point differences in J at a single threshold are dominated by finite-sample calibration variance.

strengths: Clear identification and diagnosis of the tree-gain magnitude inversion, showing across both AlphaEarth V1 and TESSERA v1 that one-year tree-gain plots have smaller median embedding changes than unchanged grass/shrub plots (AUROC 0.287-0.352).

Insightful ablation diagnostics—specifically subsequent-state similarity (b . r_b) and initial-vector-only (before-only) classifiers—that explain why differencing (b - a) degrades one-year gain detection and how much transition signal is already present before the transition year.

Exemplary statistical transparency, reporting all pre-specified comparisons, exact numerator/denominator counts, algebraic constraints, and partition sensitivities without cherry-picking positive results.

Side-by-side evaluation of two distinct satellite embedding paradigms (weakly supervised AlphaEarth V1 and self-supervised TESSERA v1) across two human-interpreted US reference datasets (LCMAP and Annual NLCD).

closest_prior_work.citation: Brown, C. F., et al. (2025). AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data. arXiv:2507.22291.
closest_prior_work.difference: Evaluated AlphaEarth angular anomaly and supervised classifiers on LCMAP land-cover change using validation-selected thresholds, whereas this paper evaluates spatially transferred thresholds separately for conditional tree gain and loss alongside reference adjustments and TESSERA v1.

closest_prior_work.citation: Heiman, A. (2026). Characterizing Brazilian Atlantic Forest Restoration Outcomes with Geospatial AlphaEarth Embeddings. arXiv:2605.05547, ICLR ML4RS Workshop.
closest_prior_work.difference: Introduced cosine similarity to mature forest reference embeddings to track multi-year restoration trajectories in Brazil, whereas this paper tests whether year-matched or control-adjusted reference similarity improves one-year tree-cover transition classification in CONUS.

closest_prior_work.citation: Feng, Z., et al. (2026). TESSERA: Temporal Embeddings of Surface Spectra for Earth Representation and Analysis. CVPR 2026 / arXiv:2506.20380.
closest_prior_work.difference: Introduced the self-supervised TESSERA annual 10m embeddings evaluated here, but did not benchmark reference-similarity adjustments or conditional one-year tree gain/loss screening on LCMAP and NLCD.

closest_prior_work.citation: Burns, M. (2026). Rethinking Change Detection and Attribution: How You Compare Satellite Embeddings Matters. Google Earth and Earth Engine Medium.
closest_prior_work.difference: Contrasted dot products, difference vectors, and stacked annual AlphaEarth embeddings retaining baseline context in a regional case study, whereas this paper performs a quantitative, spatially held-out threshold-transfer evaluation across CONUS with TESSERA v1 and explicit state/before-only controls.

closest_prior_work.citation: Sharma, A., et al. (2026). Label-Free Detection of Hidden Forest Degradation Using Sentinel-2, Landsat Thermal Stress and AlphaEarth Embeddings. Preprints.org, doi:10.20944/preprints202610.0842.v1.
closest_prior_work.difference: Fused year-to-year AlphaEarth embedding drift with Sentinel-2 and Landsat thermal indices to flag forest conversion and degradation against Dynamic World, whereas this paper isolates pure embedding change scores and supervised classifiers on human-interpreted LCMAP and NLCD reference plots.
